Ui.SourceCodeLabel: View the FluentLocalizer source code on GitHub
Ui.Tagline: Localization that reads like your code.
Ui.HeroDescription: Chain a key, a culture and a few arguments. FluentLocalizer finds the template, applies plural and select rules, and hands back a message ready for your users.
Ui.HeroVisual: A C# example that uses the Fluent API to format a greeting in English, Italian, French, German and Spanish.
Ui.FeaturesDescription: From a one-word label to a sentence that agrees in number and gender, every message is a template you can read, review and translate. No .resx files, no string concatenation.
Ui.FluentDescription: Get, WithArg, Pluralize, Resolve: every call says what it does, so a translation is as easy to review as the code around it.
Ui.NuanceDescription: Plural and select branches belong to the template, so each language applies its own rules without a single if in your code.
Ui.CultureDescription: Requests follow CurrentUICulture automatically. Override it per call, and let JSON stores fall back from en-GB to en and then to your default language.
Ui.ExtendDescription: Implement the two methods of ITranslationStore to read from any source, or use the ready-made JSON stores and the dependency injection package.
Ui.WorkflowDescription: Store one template per language. At runtime, pass the values and, if you need to, a culture. FluentLocalizer picks the template, applies that language's rules and returns the final text.
Ui.AddNeeded: Add the rest when you need it.
Ui.PackagesDescription: Three focused NuGet packages. The core has no opinion on where translations live; storage and dependency injection are opt-in.
Ui.CoreDescription: The translator, the fluent builder, ICU message formatting, options and the ITranslationStore contract.
Ui.StorageDescription: JSON catalogs from the file system, embedded resources or HTTP, with culture fallback.
Ui.IntegrationDescription: One-call registration with Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection, including options and logging.
Ui.Versions: Versions match the packages declared in this repository.

Ui.DocsDescription: From installation to your first localized message, plus how culture, fallback and stores behave at runtime.
Ui.QuickStartIntro: Install the core package, then give `Translator` an `ITranslationStore`. The store returns the raw template for a key and culture; the translator formats it with the arguments of the request, following the ICU message syntax.
Ui.SmallStore: A store implements one synchronous and one asynchronous lookup, and returns `null` when it has no template for a key. A minimal in-memory store looks like this:
Ui.ResolveExample: Then resolve a message with the current UI culture and one argument:
Ui.DefaultCulture: *The UI culture is the default.* `Get(key)` captures `CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture` when it creates the builder and uses it both to look up the template and to format it: set the UI culture once and every request follows it, with no `WithCulture(...)` call. Use `WithCulture(...)` only to force a different culture for one request; it never changes the ambient culture.
Ui.AsyncResolve: Use `ResolveAsync()` when the store does asynchronous I/O, for example when it downloads catalogs over HTTP.
Ui.PatternsDescription: Templates use the [ICU message syntax](https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/messages/). These three patterns cover most interface text and appear throughout this site and the repository samples:
Ui.InsertArgument: Inserts the value of a named argument.
Ui.PluralBranch: Picks a branch from a number with the plural rules of the request culture; `#` prints the number.
Ui.SelectBranch: Picks the branch whose name matches a text value.
Ui.PatternOther: Plural and select need an `other` branch for values without a case of their own. FluentLocalizer parses and formats templates with [MessageFormat](https://github.com/jeffijoe/messageformat.net), the open-source .NET library by Jeff Hansen: see its documentation for the ICU features it supports. The [playground](playground) runs that same formatter, so you can test a pattern before shipping it.
Ui.RequestsDescription: Each `Get(key)` call starts an independent request that you configure step by step. Argument names are case-insensitive, and a value set on the request replaces the `DefaultArguments` entry with the same name.
Ui.ChooseKey: Starts a request for a key and captures the current UI culture.
Ui.ChooseCulture: Optional: forces a culture other than the UI culture, for this request only.
Ui.SupplyArgument: Adds or replaces a named argument.
Ui.PluralizeArgument: Sets the `quantity` argument used by plural branches.
Ui.TransformResolved: Changes the letter case of the formatted text with a `LetterCase` value, such as `Upper` or `KebabCase`.
Ui.ReturnSync: Looks up and formats the message synchronously.
Ui.ResolveAsync: Looks up the template asynchronously, then formats it.
Ui.CultureSettings: Changing the culture for the whole app
Ui.ChangeCulture: To change the default for new requests, set `CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture` before calling `Get(...)`. Set `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture` too, so standard .NET number and date formatting follows the same language:
Ui.CultureScope: Builders keep the culture they captured, so create a new one after the change. The current culture belongs to the execution context and flows across `await` on modern .NET. Text cached elsewhere, or UI that is already rendered, must be refreshed by its owner.
Ui.CultureDefaults: To set a default for every thread, assign `CultureInfo.DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture` and `CultureInfo.DefaultThreadCurrentCulture` at startup; they do not override cultures set explicitly on a thread. In ASP.NET Core, set the culture per request with request localization instead of changing these process-wide defaults.
Ui.ForceCulture: `WithCulture(...)` is for the exceptions: a message that must ignore the UI culture, such as an email in the recipient's language or a page that shows several languages side by side. If every request would receive the same culture, set `CurrentUICulture` instead.
Ui.OptionsDescription: `TranslationOptions` decides what happens when a key is missing or a template cannot be formatted. By default a missing key returns the key in brackets, such as `[Home:Title]`, and a formatting error returns `[Format Error]`. You can replace either fallback with your own text, where `'{key}'` and `'{culture}'` are substituted, or throw a `TranslationException` instead.
Ui.JsonFallback: Culture fallback for JSON catalogs is configured on the store with `FallbackCulture`, which defaults to `en-US`. For a request in `it-IT`, the store looks in the `it-IT` files, then in the `it` files, then in those of the fallback culture, one key at a time. [Organizing JSON files](docs#json-files) shows how to name the files.
Ui.JsonIntro: Install `FluentLocalizer.Store.Json` to keep translations in JSON catalogs, one per culture. Nested objects become colon-separated keys: the file below defines `Home:Welcome`.
Ui.FileStore: Reads catalogs from disk; relative paths start from the application base directory. Enable `ReloadOnChange` to pick up edits without a restart.
Ui.EmbeddedStore: Reads catalogs embedded in an assembly, so they ship with your binaries. It reads one file per culture and also runs in the browser: this site uses it.
Ui.HttpStore: Downloads static catalogs over HTTP and caches them in memory. Designed for Blazor WebAssembly.
Ui.HttpUsage: With `HttpJsonStore`, publish the locale files under `wwwroot` and pass an `HttpClient` whose base address points at the site. `ResolveAsync()` downloads catalogs on demand; call `LoadAsync(...)` first if you also need the synchronous `Resolve()`:
Ui.JsonKeys: A key is a path through nested objects, with `:` between segments, and each string value is an ICU template. This file defines `Welcome`, `Checkout:Title` and `Checkout:Items`:
Ui.JsonKeyRules: Always nest objects: keys are split at every `:`, so a property named `Checkout:Title` is never found. Property names are case-sensitive and `.` has no special meaning. Only strings are templates: a key that reaches a number, an array or `null` counts as missing.
Ui.NamespaceIntro: The first segment of a key with two or more segments is its namespace: in `common:Buttons:Save` it is `common`. Keep the namespace as a top-level object of the culture file, or move it to a file of its own without the namespace object. The key stays the same:
Ui.NamespaceFiles: `JsonFileStore` and `HttpJsonStore` find the `common` namespace of `it-IT` in `it-IT.common.json`, `common.it-IT.json` or `it-IT/common.json`; culture folders are one level deep. Namespace files split large catalogs by feature and let `HttpJsonStore` download only what a page uses. `EmbeddedJsonStore` reads only the culture file, so keep namespaces inside it when you embed catalogs.
Ui.LookupDescription: For `common:Buttons:Save` in `it-IT`, the store tries a file mapped in `FileMappings`, the `common` namespace files, `it-IT.json`, then the same files for the neutral culture `it` and finally those of `FallbackCulture`. It falls back one key at a time, so regional and namespace files only need the strings that differ.
Ui.LayoutDescription: Name each language's main catalog after its neutral culture and add regional files only for the strings that differ. With `FallbackCulture` set to `en`, `it-IT`, `it-CH` and `it` all read `it.json`, `en-GB` reads `en-GB.json` before `en.json`, and any other language reads `en.json`, in every store:
Ui.RegionalWarning: With regional names only, `JsonFileStore`, and `HttpJsonStore` with a manifest, never borrow a sibling region: if only `it-IT.json` exists, a request for `it-CH` throws `FileNotFoundException` instead of falling back. Add `it.json`, or map the culture with `FileMappings["it-CH"] = "it-IT.json"`.
Ui.SiteLayout: This site follows the same layout: `en.json`, `it.json`, `fr.json`, `de.json` and `es.json`, embedded with `EmbeddedJsonStore` and `FallbackCulture` set to `en`.
Ui.InjectionDescription: `AddFluentLocalizer(...)` configures `TranslationOptions` and registers `ITranslator` as a singleton in the Microsoft dependency injection container. Choose a store with `WithStore(...)`, then inject `ITranslator` wherever you need it; `WithLogger()` forwards translation events to `ILogger`.
